newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui mutineers, peacekeepers clash, three dead.
newsitem.headline: Bangui mutineers, peacekeepers clash, three dead.

text.p: Three army mutineers were killed in the Central African Republic's capital Bangui on Saturday in clashes with African peacekeepers, a spokesman for the peacekeepers said.
The clashes were the most serious since President Ange-Felix Patasse and his rivals agreed an African-mediated peace plan in January to end the country's third army mutiny in under a year.

The spokesman told Reuters the peacekeepers, who took over from French troops last month to act as a buffer between the rival forces, had opened fire in self-defence after mutineers fired on them. He reported several people wounded.
The peacekeepers intervened after mutineers tried to loot petrol, he said.
Residents said the sound of gunshots, including heavy weapons fire, could be heard in the capital for much of the day. Calm returned later.
The first mutinies last April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian who won 1993 presidential elections.
The latest mutiny, which began on November 15, degenerated into ethnic bloodshed. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order.
The conflict opposed the mutineers, mainly southerners from the minority Yakoma tribe of former military ruler Andre Kolingba, and Patasse's presidential guard.
All eight soldiers and 11 civilians still detained after the latest unrest were released on March 17 under an amnesty.
The amnesty, signed by Patasse, gave all mutineers until March 30 to hand over their weapons or fail to qualify.
Patasse formed a government of national unity under the peace deal but his supporters hold the main portfolios. Friction has continued between Patasse and the mutineers.
Witnesses had reported sporadic gunfire from rebel strongholds earlier this month.
